questions.def: "Roundly" means thoroughly or severely, fitting before the verb.
questions.question: The report was ___ criticized for its lack of detail.

questions.def: "Infrequently" is an adverb showing how often she visits.
questions.question: She visits her parents ___.

questions.def: "Already" conflicts with "scarcely"; use a different adverb.
questions.question: He has scarcely eaten already today.

questions.def: An adverb is needed to modify the whole sentence here.
questions.question: ___, the error was discovered before publication.

questions.def: "Scarcely" is best for inverted structures with "than."
questions.question: ___ had she finished her speech than the applause began.

questions.def: "Unanimously" describes how the committee approved it.
questions.question: The committee ___ approved the proposal.

questions.def: "Only" should be before "an apple" to modify it.
questions.question: She only had eaten an apple.

questions.def: An adverb is needed to modify the verb "explained."
questions.question: The instructions were not ___ explained.

questions.def: "Eloquently" describes the manner of his speaking.
questions.question: He spoke ___ about the need for reform.

questions.def: "Undeniably" modifies how compelling the evidence was.
questions.question: The evidence was ___ compelling.

questions.def: Adverb of frequency 'seldom' goes before 'are' in this case.
questions.question: They seldom are on time.

questions.def: "Equally" modifies the adjective "challenging."
questions.question: The task was ___ challenging for all participants.

questions.def: "Hastily" describes how the decision was made.
questions.question: The decision was ___ made, without proper consultation.

questions.def: "Occasionally" is an adverb of frequency.
questions.question: The museum ___ opens on weekends.

questions.def: "Very" goes before "talented" and after "is."
questions.question: She very is talented musician.

questions.def: "Wisely" describes how he chose to act.
questions.question: He ___ chose to remain silent.

questions.def: "Forthrightly" describes how he admitted his error.
questions.question: He ___ admitted his mistake.

questions.def: "Exceedingly" modifies how enjoyable the concert was.
questions.question: The concert was ___ enjoyable.

questions.def: "Nearly" should be after "all" in this context.
questions.question: They nearly all have finished.

questions.def: "Clearly" describes how the problem was identified.
questions.question: The problem was ___ identified.

questions.def: "Intuitively" describes how she understood the equation.
questions.question: She ___ understood the complex equation.

questions.def: "Unaccountably" means without explanation for being late.
questions.question: He was ___ late for the meeting.

questions.def: "Rather" should be after 'is' in this sentence.
questions.question: She rather is a perfectionist.

questions.def: "Readily" describes how he accepted the challenge.
questions.question: He ___ accepted the challenge.

questions.def: "Unexpectedly" modifies the whole clause regarding completion.
questions.question: The project was ___ completed ahead of schedule.

questions.def: "Impeccably" describes the quality of the formatting.
questions.question: The document was ___ formatted.

questions.def: "Already" is redundant because "have been gone" indicates completion.
questions.question: They have already been gone.

questions.def: "Actually" emphasizes his presence at the scene.
questions.question: He was ___ present at the scene.

questions.def: "Rigorously" describes the manner of analysis.
questions.question: The data was ___ analyzed.

questions.def: "Reluctantly" describes how she agreed.
questions.question: She ___ agreed to the terms.
